stem_book: Assertion–Reason (i) to (iii). (a) If assertion is true but the reason is false. (b) If assertion is false but reason is true. (c) If both assertion and reason are true and the reason is the correct explanation of assertion. (d) If both assertion and reason are true but reason is not the correct explanation of assertion. (i) Assertion: Multiple bond between two bonded atoms can have more than three bonds. Reason: Multiple bond between two bonded atoms can not have more than two π-bonds. (ii) Assertion: In SO₃ molecule bond dissociation energy of all S=O bonds are not equivalent. Reason: SO₃ molecule is having two types of 2pπ–3pπ and 2pπ–3dπ pi-bonds. (iii) Assertion: The atoms in a covalent molecule are said to share electrons, yet some covalent molecules are polar. Reason: In polar covalent molecule, the shared electrons spend more time on the average near one of the atoms.
reason: Three separate assertion–reason items under one number; the manifest lists them as three entries under this one code. (i) rests on quadruple (σ+2π+δ) bonds like Re₂Cl₈²⁻ — arguable for JEE.
work: (i) quadruple bond σ+2π+δ: A true, R true, unrelated; (ii) resonance makes all S—O in SO₃ equal ⇒ A false, R true; (iii) unequal sharing ⇒ dipole ⇒ c
